title: Developers completed a coding task sooner
date_precision: The paper reports an experiment from May 15 to June 20, 2022. Its recruitment figure separately dates the Upwork posting to May 25.
location: Remote participants recruited through Upwork, mainly in India and Pakistan
observed_outcome: Among developers who finished the task, those assigned GitHub Copilot completed a JavaScript HTTP server in 55.8% less time, averaging 71.17 versus 160.89 minutes.
ai_contribution: Suggested code and functions while developers wrote the server.
human_contribution: Developers implemented and submitted the program. They could use web search and other usual resources. A fixed suite checked twelve required behaviors.
evidence_supports: 95 developers were randomized, 45 to Copilot and 50 to control. The completion-time comparison covers 35 successful participants per group. The reported 95% confidence interval for the reduction is 21–89%.
limitations: One bounded JavaScript task. Completion-time results condition on successful completion. The success-rate difference was not statistically significant. The study did not evaluate broader code quality, security, maintenance, or team productivity. Authors included GitHub and Microsoft employees.
tradeoffs: Passing the twelve task tests does not establish secure, maintainable production code. Those properties were outside the evaluation.
replication_hypothesis: The task supplied a starter repository, explicit requirements, automatic tests, a brief tool introduction, and incentives for speed. Applicability to larger projects remains unestablished.
beneficiaries: Professional developers completing the tested coding assignment.
stakeholder_detail: 95 Upwork recruits were assigned. Seventy completed the task and survey. Faster completion is not proof of higher earnings or a benefit for every assigned developer.

sources.title: The Impact of AI on Developer Productivity: Evidence from GitHub Copilot
sources.authors: Sida Peng, Eirini Kalliamvakou, Peter Cihon, and Mert Demirer

evidence_basis.evidence_design: Random assignment to Copilot access for a single incentivized programming task.
evidence_basis.reported_by: Peng and colleagues, including GitHub and Microsoft researchers
evidence_basis.outcome_documentation: Repository timestamps measured elapsed time until the first submission passing all twelve tests. The reported time effect is conditional on completion.
evidence_basis.verification_limit: Primary preprint reviewed. Peer review is not established from the arXiv record. Authors include tool-provider employees. No independent replication is established.

ai_attribution: The study compares assignment to Copilot plus a short introduction with no Copilot access. Five treatment-assigned participants did not finish tool signup.
editorial_classification_note: Describe the result as shorter completion time among successful participants. Do not convert it into a whole-job productivity gain, code-quality improvement, or successful career transition.

system_details.source_note: The paper identifies Codex and evaluates Copilot before general availability in June 2022. It gives no exact Codex snapshot or extension version.

reporting_period.display: May 15–June 20, 2022, as reported in Study Design

denominators.notes: Five treatment-assigned participants did not finish Copilot signup. The completion-time contrast is conditional on finishing.

measurements.measure: Mean completion time among successful participants
Reduction in completion time among successful participants

research_data.duration_follow_up: One coding assignment. No longitudinal productivity or maintenance outcome.
limitations: Broader code quality and production work unmeasured.
research_data.source_notes: Study Design, Results, Figure 6, and Discussion. The text’s May 15 start and Figure 1’s May 25 posting date are preserved without reconciling them by inference.
research_data.evidence_status: Primary research preprint reviewed. Peer review and independent replication are not established.
